accuracy.evidence: Checked against AQA A-level Chemistry 7405 specification 3.1.6.1 (Le Chatelier's principle; effects of concentration, pressure and temperature on position; catalysts do not affect position; the compromise in industrial processes), OCR A 3.2.3, Chemguide 'The Haber process' and 'Le Chatelier's principle', and the RSC Learn Chemistry Haber process notes. ΔH = −92 kJ/mol, ~450 °C, ~200 atm, iron catalyst, ~15% per pass with recycling, 2NO₂ ⇌ N₂O₄ ΔH = −57 kJ/mol and 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ ΔH = −196 kJ/mol all match those sources. The lab is an exact constant-volume Kc solve; ln Kp is fitted through the classic ideal-gas Kp values 1.64×10⁻⁴ atm⁻² (400 °C) and 1.45×10⁻⁵ atm⁻² (500 °C), giving 4.5×10⁻⁵ at 450 °C and an equilibrium NH₃ fraction of 24.7% at 450 °C/200 atm, consistent with Chemguide's yield chart. Constant volume is used deliberately so that adding N₂ always shifts right (at constant total pressure that can fail at high N₂ fractions). The rate on the map is labelled a model (Ea taken as 100 kJ/mol) and only used to compare temperatures.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented A-level errors (Quílez & Solaz 1995 and Quílez 2004 on Le Chatelier misapplication; Banerjee 1991; RSC 'Chemical misconceptions' equilibrium probes; AQA examiner reports): higher temperature gives more product because the rate rises, catalysts raise yield, pressure counted over all species including solids, concentration or pressure changes alter K, adding a reactant 'shifts left to make room', and 'no equilibrium exists at low temperature'. Each is a prediction option or a tagged challenge answer with its own message.

lab_distinct.evidence: flaglechat is a perturbation lab on one real system: a pistoned flask whose amounts glide to a new exact equilibrium, a log Q/K gauge, a draggable thermometer that changes Kc, a catalyst race to the same plateau, and a temperature–pressure yield map with a cost line. flagequil (the prerequisite) runs A ⇌ B particles to equilibrium with rate constants and one 'open flask' step; it has no Q/K gauge, no temperature dependence of K, no pressure or gas-count effect and no compromise map. Shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step shows the cause before the rule is confirmed: after adding N₂ the gauge marker jumps left of centre (Q < K) and then returns as NH₃ rises, so 'shift to oppose' is seen as Q returning to K; dragging the thermometer changes the Kc readout while the amounts are still unchanged, showing that only temperature moves K; squeezing the piston raises NH₃ from 24.0% to 33.8% with Kc fixed; the catalyst curves meet the same dashed line; the map's feedback names which of yield, rate or cost fails at the chosen point.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: adding N₂ 'shifts left, to make room' or 'does not move, because K stays the same'; heating 'rises, because hotter reactions go faster'; halving the volume 'falls: more pressure pushes molecules apart' or 'stays the same: K has not changed'; a catalyst makes the yield 'bigger'; plants run hot because 'the yield is higher when hot'. The completion line names the learner's choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions on other equilibria (NO₂/N₂O₄ cooling and heating, H₂ + I₂ pressure, catalyst, NH₃ removal, CaCO₃ with solids, the 200 °C option). Wrong answers carry tags with distinct messages: temp (check the sign of ΔH), gas (count gas molecules only; equal numbers means no shift), K (temperature does shift position and alters K), Kconc (concentration and pressure leave K unchanged), cat (both directions sped up equally), conc (removing product makes Q < K), eq (equilibrium still exists at 200 °C, reached too slowly).

readability.evidence: Learner kid explanation FK grade 4.1 (paragraphs 2.7–5.9) and adult 9.2, inside the 6.5 / 9.5 limits. Precise A-level terms are kept and used correctly: position of equilibrium, reaction quotient Q, equilibrium constant K/Kc, exothermic/endothermic direction, closed system, compromise conditions. Lab step text is two or three short sentences.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs each carry one factor (principle; concentration with Q and K; pressure with gas counting; temperature, K and catalysts). The adult text gives specification links, the Haber numbers with the recycling point, four named mistakes and the lab walk-through. No filler phrase matched; the 12% duplicate gate passed against lesson 612 dynamic equilibrium.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of every step in both themes (shots/lc-phone-t0/t1, mid-lc-*): flask, bars and thermometer sit side by side at 390 px without overlap; the gauge labels fit; the map's axis labels were de-cluttered during review (the 350 atm tick collided with the 'atm' title) and canvas text was raised to 12–13 px minimum; long feedback wraps onto up to three lines; all controls are buttons under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passes: axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean on desktop and iPhone 13 in light and dark, no console errors, all 5 tasks complete with Show me. Every drag has a button twin: Add 1 mol N₂ / Condense, five temperature buttons, three volume buttons, two catalyst runs, four ±25 °C / ±50 atm map buttons plus 'Check these conditions'. The canvas aria-label and live region read each result, the volume while dragging the piston and the temperature while dragging the thermometer.
